title: Free and cofree evaluation for specified inverse-image coherence
statement: Let I be a small category, D a VaryingSiteDiagram and e a VaryingSiteCoherence [def-per-varying-site-system]. In particular every inverse image is additive and preserves finite limits, and e satisfies the two unit and associativity identities. For each vertex i there exists L_i:Ab(C_i)→S with L_i left adjoint to evaluation ev_i and preserving monomorphisms, and there exists R_i:Ab(C_i)→S right adjoint to ev_i. Here S is the category VaryingSiteSystem D e with arbitrary, possibly noninvertible, transition maps. No site-level pseudofunctor or compatibility of e with a separately chosen site compositor is assumed.

source.place: Tags 09WG (5)-(7) and 09WH, free evaluation construction, generalized to arbitrary small categories and specified inverse-image coherence; cofree construction from sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0EXZ.

proof.text: Each D.pull a is the actual left adjoint of continuous sheaf pushforward. Products of sheaves are sectionwise and coproducts are sheafifications of sectionwise presheaf coproducts. For a fixed i and A put (L_i A)_j=⊕_{a:j→i}(D.pull a)(A). Preservation of coproducts by D.pull c defines the transition on the a-summand using the inverse of e.comp c a and the (c≫a)-inclusion. Test identity and cocycle on all summands; exactly the unit and associativity axioms of e give these identities. The same formula on arrows is functorial.

source.place: Tags 09WG (5)-(7) and 09WH, free evaluation construction, generalized to arbitrary small categories and specified inverse-image coherence; cofree construction from sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0EXZ.

proof.text: A map A→F_i extends on the a-summand by inverse image followed by F.transition a. The cocycle makes it compatible; restriction to the identity summand, transported with e.unit, is the inverse. Compatibility with each a recovers the corresponding summand, including nonidentity endomorphisms. The formulas commute with pre- and postcomposition, yielding the adjunction by natural Hom bijections. Every inverse image preserves monomorphisms by D.exact_limits. A coproduct of such monomorphisms is monic because finite subsums are monic and the full sum is their filtered colimit, which is exact in abelian sheaves. A componentwise monic compatible family is monic, by componentwise cancellation. Hence L_i preserves monomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 09WG (5)-(7) and 09WH, free evaluation construction, generalized to arbitrary small categories and specified inverse-image coherence; cofree construction from sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0EXZ.

proof.text: Take the mates of e.unit and e.comp under the actual sheaf adjunctions. The Hom bijections for composite adjunctions show that these direct-image comparisons satisfy the unit and associativity equations. Put (R_i A)_j=∏_{a:i→j}P_a A, where P_a is direct image. For c:k→j define the transposed transition into P_c((R_i A)_k) by its b:i→k projection: it is the (b≫c)-projection transported by the mate compositor. Right adjoints preserve products, so this defines it uniquely. Projection tests and the mate coherence prove identity and cocycle; transposition supplies the inverse-image transitions. Products also define R_i on arrows and prove its functor laws.

source.place: Tag 0EXZ, lemma-colim-sites-injective, category of systems; agent generalization to specified coherent inverse images over any small category.

proof.text: For h:F_i→A define F→R_i A by taking the a:i→j projection to be the adjunct of F.transition a≫h. After transposition the cocycle proves compatibility by testing every projection. The inverse is the identity-factor projection with the mate unit comparison. Compatibility with each a recovers every projection of the original map; starting from h recovers h by the identity law. Product uniqueness proves both inverse identities. These formulas are natural, giving ev_i⊣R_i. Empty Hom sets give zero sheaves, and empty I requires no construction at a vertex.

from.place: The passage from finite-stage Leray to the limit spectral sequence in ILO XX 4.4, used in the completion part of proof Step 3 of the blueprint ancestor. This node isolates free and cofree evaluation for specified inverse-image coherence, used in the system-resolution argument.

lean.statement: theorem varyingSiteSystem_evaluation_adjoints {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] (D : VaryingSiteDiagram.{u} I) (e : VaryingSiteCoherence D) (i : I) : (∃ L : D.Ab i ⥤ VaryingSiteSystem D e, Nonempty (L ⊣ VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i) ∧ L.PreservesMonomorphisms) ∧ (∃ R : D.Ab i ⥤ VaryingSiteSystem D e, Nonempty (VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i ⊣ R))
